chunks: Muhammad ibn Muslim said: I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying:
The absent man and the absent woman — there is no stoning upon them both, except if the man happens to be with the woman and the woman with the man.

key_terms.الإحصان: ihsan — the legal condition of being in an active, consummated marriage; a prerequisite for rajm
key_terms.الْمُغِيبَةُ: al-mughibah — a woman whose husband is absent or has been away for an extended period
key_terms.الْمُغِيبُ: al-mughib — a man whose wife is absent or has been away for an extended period; from ghayb (absence)
key_terms.رَجْمٌ: rajm — stoning, the hadd punishment for adultery (zina) when the person is muhsan (married with conjugal access)

ai.seo_question: Does a married person whose spouse is absent face stoning for adultery according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: This hadith from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) establishes an important condition for the hadd punishment of stoning (rajm): that the married person must have actual access to their spouse. If a person's spouse is absent or away, they are not considered fully 'muhsan' (in the protected conjugal state that triggers rajm) because cohabitation and conjugal access are preconditions. This ruling protects individuals whose spouses have been absent for extended periods from the severest punishment, reflecting the principle that hadd punishments require the full conditions of ihsan to be met — including actual, not merely nominal, marital cohabitation.
word_analysis: the absent man (whose wife is away)
and the absent woman (whose husband is away)

en.hubeali:
Ali, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Abu Ayoub Al Khazaz, from Muhammad Bin Muslim who said, 
‘I heard Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> saying:
‘The absent man and the absent woman, there is no stoning upon them both, except if the man happens to be with the woman, and the woman with the man’.
